html:
AnyCalib (University of Zaragoza, ICCV 2025): the camera of one photo (focal length, principal point, field of view) from one predicted viewing ray per pixel and a fit; no checkerboard needed, no gravity. Apache-2.0 code and weights; trained on crops of public 360-degree panoramas.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Paper: AnyCalib: On-Manifold Learning for Model-Agnostic Single-View Camera Calibration, ICCV 2025, 2025-03-16
  • Original code: https://github.com/javrtg/AnyCalib at 027a8497d893
  • Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: Apache-2.0
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/javrtg/AnyCalib/blob/027a8497d893f4b2596f23d6324c05e4b81064ed/LICENSE ; https://github.com/javrtg/AnyCalib/blob/027a8497d893f4b2596f23d6324c05e4b81064ed/README.md
  • Training data: LVD-142M (DINOv2's curated web-image set, not released), OpenPano (perspective crops of public 360-degree panoramas: PolyHaven, HDRMaps, AmbientCG, BlenderKit) (anycalib_pinhole: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 (LVD-142M) fine-tuned on the perspective OpenPano split (OP_p; README, paper Sec. 5). Only the weights licence counts for the commercial flag.)
  • Options: cuda_graphs = True (speed only)
  • Kernel libraries: fastbb, dpt_fused, cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: anycalib-pinhole
  • Outputs: intrinsics, vfov
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): anycalib-pinhole 3000x4000 (1.0 GiB peak allocated, 1.1 reserved)
  • anycalib-pinhole 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 17 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • anycalib-pinhole original 1080x1920: torch.autocast(float16) around the call; javrtg/AnyCalib@027a8497d893 AnyCalib.predict (pinhole), its resize / crop / linear + GN fit
  • anycalib-pinhole load / first call: original 4.09 s / 0.578 s, portable 0.6 s / 0.452 s, kernels 1.59 s / 0.329 s
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Each image at its own size (1440 x 1920 portrait); roll, pitch and vertical field of view of the fitted camera against the ground truth; AUC of the error up to 5 degrees (errors below 1 degree count as 1, siclib's compute_auc(min_error=1)), the GeoCalib paper's protocol. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.
